rationale: C22 is a highly plausible material drafting template. It predates the child by about six weeks and uses virtually the same complete structure and wording: a dispute between a named railroad and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen; the identical Railway Labor Act and National Mediation Board findings; the same thirty-day reporting requirement; and the same section 10 prohibition on changing the conditions underlying the dispute. The principal adaptations are the railroad name and the geographic characterization of the threatened interruption. C12 and C01 are also strong instances of the same template, but C22 most closely matches the child in recency, party configuration, and represented union.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS a dispute exists between the Boston & Albany Railroad Company (New York Central R.R. Company, Lessee), a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS a dispute exists between the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization
shared_material.explanation: The opening clause has the same detailed syntactic frame and the same employee organization, with the named railroad substituted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and WHEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation service
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and WHEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the national Mediation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a large section of the country of essential transportation service
shared_material.explanation: The two predicate findings are nearly verbatim; the only substantive wording change is from “a large section” to “a section.”

shared_material.child_excerpt: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to the said dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Boston & Albany Railroad Company or its employees in the conditions out of which the said dispute arose.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company or its employees in the conditions out of which the said dispute arose.
shared_material.explanation: The operative section 10 machinery is reproduced verbatim apart from substitution of the railroad name.
